claims.text: A release train releases changes on fixed, published dates: whatever is ready when the train leaves goes, and anything not ready waits for the next train instead of delaying it.

ADR 0019 sends api changes through canary steps (Notifications and Payments roll out with a rolling update) and puts changes customers see behind a feature flag that is off, turned on per feature-flags.md.
The calendar plans for 1,000 shops (marked as an assumption in the file).
A train runs at the end of every two-week sprint, only for changes shops can see; releasing means turning on the change's feature flag per feature-flags.md, not deploying.
Code still reaches production on any day through the canary of ADR 0019 with the flag off; deploying is the team's business, releasing is what shops are told about in advance.
claims.source_hint: docs/team/release-calendar.md @ stage-4 lines 16-18; docs/design/feature-flags.md @ stage-4 section 'Flag và lịch phát hành'

claims.text: Changes shops cannot see (internal fixes, library upgrades, platform work) do not ride the train; they go to production when done.

The release note reaches shops 5 working days before the train so they can prepare staff and customers; a change not in production, not through every canary step, or not in the note by then takes the next train.
The train does not move its date to wait for a late change because shops were already told the date; the product owner fixes the list of changes for each train.

At stage-4 the Đơn Hàng API has no feature flag yet; FeatureFlags lives in samples/DonHang.Samples. The calendar is a convention for the first feature shops will see and later ones, not something already running.
claims.source_hint: docs/team/release-calendar.md @ stage-4 lines 3-5; docs/design/feature-flags.md @ stage-4 lines 1-8

claims.text: Incident and vulnerability fixes do not wait for a train; the calendar calls shipping one a release outside the calendar. During an incident the incident commander (incident-response.md) may release; for a vulnerability fix not tied to an incident, the team lead may.

An out-of-calendar api fix still goes through the canary of ADR 0019 even when the error budget in slo.md is spent; affected shops are told the same day what was fixed and whether they must act, and the next train's note records it.
claims.source_hint: docs/team/release-calendar.md @ stage-4 lines 38-42; ADR 0019 section Hệ quả

claims.text: A breaking change for shops is announced at least two trains ahead, in the release notes of both trains.

A change that misses a train waits two weeks for the next; readiness is judged when the note goes out, 5 working days earlier, so one finished just after a note waits close to three weeks. The file itself (lines 52-53) says 'up to two weeks'.

Moving the train's date for one change breaks the shops' plan for every change on the train and every shop; a date that slips repeatedly makes shops stop preparing. Shops need a fix as soon as it exists, not behind a flag until a train.

Trade-offs: a train fits when many users must prepare and deploys can run apart from releases; turning each change on when done fits when users need no preparation; a date waiting on one feature moves when it runs late and fits rarely.

Not written in Đơn Hàng's files: with three-week sprints a change missing a train waits three weeks, nearly four if finished just after a note; a team should check with shops whether that wait is still acceptable.
Piling two weeks of changes into one deploy on train day means one failure blocks every change at once.
Only one team works on the whole Đơn Hàng system; the train exists because many shops must prepare, not to line up the work of several teams.
Under this calendar a train need not lower how often the team deploys, because code still reaches production any day.
In Đơn Hàng's calendar the code of a change shops can see reaches production any day through the canary with its flag off; the train only decides when the flag is turned on.
ADR 0019 uses a canary for api changes; Notifications and Payments roll out with a rolling update.
